title: The Laplace Transform, Step Forcing & Convolution

sections.heading: The Laplace Transform, Step Forcing & Convolution Practice Exercises

questions.q: Find \( \mathcal L\{3 t + \cos{\left(t \right)}\} \).
questions.answer: Use the table (and linearity): \( \mathcal L\{3 t + \cos{\left(t \right)}\}=\frac{s^{3} + 3 s^{2} + 3}{s^{4} + s^{2}} \).

questions.q: Using the definition, \( \mathcal L\{e^{2 t}\}=\int_0^\infty e^{-(s-2)t}\,dt \) equals (for \( s>2 \)):
questions.answer: Evaluate the improper integral; the boundary term at infinity vanishes for \( s>2 \), leaving \( \frac{1}{s - 2} \).

questions.q: Find \( \mathcal L\{t^{4}\} \).
questions.answer: Use the table (and linearity): \( \mathcal L\{t^{4}\}=\frac{24}{s^{5}} \).

questions.q: Using the definition, \( \mathcal L\{2 t\}=\int_0^\infty 2te^{-st}\,dt \) equals (for \( s>0 \)):
questions.answer: Evaluate the improper integral; the boundary term at infinity vanishes for \( s>0 \), leaving \( \frac{2}{s^{2}} \).

questions.q: The second-order linear homogeneous ODE \( f''(x) - 53f'(x) + 696f(x) = 0 \) has characteristic roots \( \lambda_1, \lambda_2 \). What is the trace sum \( \lambda_1 + \lambda_2 \)?
questions.answer: From \( \lambda^2 - 53\lambda + 696 = 0 \), the sum of roots is \( 53 \).

questions.q: If \( \mathcal L\{y\}=Y(s) \) and \( y(0)=1 \), find \( \mathcal L\{y'\} \).
Find \( \mathcal L\{t^{3}\} \).
questions.answer: Use the table (and linearity): \( \mathcal L\{t^{3}\}=\frac{6}{s^{4}} \).

questions.q: Consider the differential equation \(y''(t) + 4y(t) = u(t-2)\), where \(u(t)\) is the Heaviside step function, with initial conditions \(y(0) = 0\) and \(y'(0) = 0\). Apply the Laplace Transform to both sides of the equation. If \(Y(s) = \mathcal{L}\{y(t)\}\) and \(\mathcal{L}\{u(t-a)\} = \frac{e^{-as}}{s}\), which of the following expressions represents \(Y(s)\)?
questions.answer: Applying the Laplace Transform to the given differential equation: \(\mathcal{L}\{y''(t)\} + 4\mathcal{L}\{y(t)\} = \mathcal{L}\{u(t-2)\}\). Using the properties of the Laplace Transform and the given initial conditions \(y(0) = 0\) and \(y'(0) = 0\), we have \(\mathcal{L}\{y''(t)\} = s^2 Y(s) - sy(0) - y'(0) = s^2 Y(s)\). The Laplace Transform of \(y(t)\) is \(Y(s)\). The Laplace Transform of the Heaviside step function \(u(t-2)\) is \(\frac{e^{-2s}}{s}\). Substituting these into the transformed equation gives: \(s^2 Y(s) + 4 Y(s) = \frac{e^{-2s}}{s}\). Factoring out \(Y(s)\), we get \(Y(s)(s^2 + 4) = \frac{e^{-2s}}{s}\). Solving for \(Y(s)\), we obtain \(Y(s) = \frac{e^{-2s}}{s(s^2 + 4)}\).

questions.q: The second-order linear homogeneous ODE \( f''(x) - 39f'(x) + 350f(x) = 0 \) has characteristic roots \( \lambda_1, \lambda_2 \). Determine the trace sum \( \lambda_1 + \lambda_2 \).
questions.answer: From \( \lambda^2 - 39\lambda + 350 = 0 \), the sum of roots is \( 39 \).

questions.q: Consider the initial value problem \( y'' + 4y = \delta(t- \pi) \) with \( y(0) = 0 \) and \( y'(0) = 0 \). Which of the following represents the Laplace Transform of the solution, \(Y(s) = \mathcal{L}\{y(t)\}\)?
questions.answer: Taking the Laplace transform of the differential equation, we have \(s^2 Y(s) - sy(0) - y'(0) + 4Y(s) = \mathcal{L}\{\delta(t-\pi)\}\). Given the initial conditions \(y(0)=0\) and \(y'(0)=0\), this simplifies to \(s^2 Y(s) + 4Y(s) = e^{-\pi s}\). Factoring out \(Y(s)\), we get \(Y(s)(s^2 + 4) = e^{-\pi s}\). Therefore, the Laplace transform of the solution is \(Y(s) = \frac{e^{-\pi s}}{s^2 + 4}\).

questions.q: The separable initial value problem \( \dfrac{df}{dx} = 40x \) satisfies \( f(0) = 4 \). Determine the solution value \( f(16) \).
questions.answer: Integrating gives \( f(x) = 20x^2 + 4 \), so \( f(16) = 5124 \).

questions.q: A damped spring satisfies \( y''+2y'+10y=0 \), \( y(0)=0 \), \( y'(0)=6 \). Find \( y(\pi/6) \).

questions.answer: Homogeneous: \( r^2+4r+4=(r+2)^2=0\Rightarrow r=-2 \) (repeated), \( y_c=(C_1+C_2x)e^{-2x} \). The forcing \( e^{-2x} \) matches the repeated root, so the trial needs \( x^2 \): \( y_p=Ax^2e^{-2x} \). Substituting gives \( 2Ae^{-2x}=e^{-2x}\Rightarrow A=\tfrac12 \), so \( y_p=\tfrac12x^2e^{-2x} \). With both conditions zero, \( C_1=C_2=0 \). So \( y=\tfrac12x^2e^{-2x} \), and \( y(2)=\tfrac12(4)e^{-4}=2e^{-4} \).

questions.q: Calculate the solution set for \( y''-7y'+12y=0 \), \( y(0)=0 \), \( y'(0)=3 \). Find \( y(1) \).
questions.answer: Auxiliary equation \( r^2-7r+12=0 \) has roots \( r=4,3 \), so \( y=C_1e^{4x}+C_2e^{3x} \). Solving \( y(0)=C_1+C_2=0 \) and \( y'(0)=4C_1+3C_2=3 \) gives \( C_1=3 \), \( C_2=-3 \). So \( y=3e^{4x}-3e^{3x} \), and \( y(1) \) follows by substitution.

Auxiliary equation \( r^2+r-2=0 \) has roots \( r=1,-2 \), so \( y=C_1e^{x}+C_2e^{-2x} \). Solving \( y(0)=C_1+C_2=0 \) and \( y'(0)=C_1-2C_2=-6 \) gives \( C_1=-2 \), \( C_2=2 \). So \( y=-2e^{x}+2e^{-2x} \), and \( y(1) \) follows by substitution.

questions.q: Find the root(s) satisfying \( y''-2y'+y=0 \), \( y(0)=1 \), \( y'(0)=2 \). Find \( y(1) \).
questions.answer: Auxiliary equation \( r^2-2r+1=0\Rightarrow(r-1)^2=0\Rightarrow r=1 \) (repeated), so \( y=(C_1+C_2x)e^{x} \). \( y(0)=C_1=1 \); \( y'(0)=C_2+C_1=2\Rightarrow C_2=1 \). So \( y=(1+x)e^{x} \), and \( y(1) \) follows by substitution.

Auxiliary equation \( r^2+9=0 \) has roots \( r=0\pm3i \), so \( y=C_1\cos3x+C_2\sin3x \). \( y(0)=C_1=-3 \); \( y'(0)=3C_2=6\Rightarrow C_2=2 \). Evaluating at \( x=\frac{\pi}{3} \) (where \( 3x=\pi \)) gives the result.

questions.q: Calculate the solution set for \( y''+4y=0 \), \( y(0)=-2 \), \( y'(0)=6 \). Find \( y(\frac{\pi}{2}) \).
questions.answer: Auxiliary equation \( r^2+4=0 \) has roots \( r=0\pm2i \), so \( y=C_1\cos2x+C_2\sin2x \). \( y(0)=C_1=-2 \); \( y'(0)=2C_2=6\Rightarrow C_2=3 \). Evaluating at \( x=\frac{\pi}{2} \) (where \( 2x=\pi \)) gives the result.

Auxiliary equation \( r^2-4r+3=0 \) has roots \( r=1,3 \), so \( y=C_1e^{x}+C_2e^{3x} \). Solving \( y(0)=C_1+C_2=-5 \) and \( y'(0)=C_1+3C_2=-7 \) gives \( C_1=-4 \), \( C_2=-1 \). So \( y=-4e^{x}-e^{3x} \), and \( y(1) \) follows by substitution.

questions.q: Find the root(s) satisfying \( y''+3y'+2y=0 \), \( y(0)=5 \), \( y'(0)=-7 \). Find \( y(2) \).
questions.answer: Auxiliary equation \( r^2+3r+2=0 \) has roots \( r=-2,-1 \), so \( y=C_1e^{-2x}+C_2e^{-x} \). Solving \( y(0)=C_1+C_2=5 \) and \( y'(0)=-2C_1-C_2=-7 \) gives \( C_1=2 \), \( C_2=3 \). So \( y=2e^{-2x}+3e^{-x} \), and \( y(2) \) follows by substitution.

questions.q: Determine the solution to \( y''-6y'+9y=0 \), \( y(0)=2 \), \( y'(0)=8 \). Find \( y(2) \).
questions.answer: Auxiliary equation \( r^2-6r+9=0\Rightarrow(r-3)^2=0\Rightarrow r=3 \) (repeated), so \( y=(C_1+C_2x)e^{3x} \). \( y(0)=C_1=2 \); \( y'(0)=C_2+3C_1=8\Rightarrow C_2=2 \). So \( y=(2+2x)e^{3x} \), and \( y(2) \) follows by substitution.

questions.q: Work out the solution to \( y''+6y'+9y=0 \), \( y(0)=-2 \), \( y'(0)=3 \). Find \( y(1) \).
questions.answer: Auxiliary equation \( r^2+6r+9=0\Rightarrow(r+3)^2=0\Rightarrow r=-3 \) (repeated), so \( y=(C_1+C_2x)e^{-3x} \). \( y(0)=C_1=-2 \); \( y'(0)=C_2-3C_1=3\Rightarrow C_2=-3 \). So \( y=(-2-3x)e^{-3x} \), and \( y(1) \) follows by substitution.

Auxiliary equation \( r^2-4r+8=0 \) has roots \( r=2\pm2i \), so \( y=e^{2x}(C_1\cos2x+C_2\sin2x) \). \( y(0)=C_1=-1 \); \( y'(0)=2C_1+2C_2=2\Rightarrow C_2=2 \). Evaluating at \( x=\frac{\pi}{6} \) (where \( 2x=\frac{\pi}{3} \)) gives the result.

Auxiliary equation \( r^2-12r+35=0 \) has roots \( r=5,7 \), so \( y=C_1e^{5x}+C_2e^{7x} \). Solving \( y(0)=C_1+C_2=-1 \) and \( y'(0)=5C_1+7C_2=-13 \) gives \( C_1=3 \), \( C_2=-4 \). So \( y=3e^{5x}-4e^{7x} \), and \( y(2) \) follows by substitution.
